title: Joshua 18:1–10
context: Israel assembles at Shiloh and sets up the Tent of Meeting there. Seven tribes have not yet received their inheritance, and Joshua rebukes their delay. Surveyors are sent to write a description of the land in seven portions, and Joshua casts lots before the LORD at Shiloh.

verses.text: The whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled themselves together at Shiloh, and set up the Tent of Meeting there. The land was subdued before them.
verses.arminianNotes: The whole congregation gathers at Shiloh and sets up the Tent of Meeting. Arminian readers see worship placed at the center of the settled life of the nation, inviting each tribe to orient its life around God’s presence.
verses.reformedNotes: Shiloh becomes the place of God’s dwelling for a long period (1 Samuel 1-4), though Jeremiah 7:12 and Psalm 78:60 later recall its loss as a warning. Reformed readers see God’s presence as the true center of the inheritance, more important than the land itself.

verses.text: Seven tribes remained among the children of Israel, which had not yet divided their inheritance.
verses.arminianNotes: Seven tribes had not yet received their inheritance, even though the land had been subdued. Arminian readers note the gap between what God had given and what the people had actually taken up.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers observe that God’s gift was secure, yet the tribes had not acted on it. The verse sets up Joshua’s rebuke and shows that God’s sovereign provision calls for his people’s active response.

verses.text: Joshua said to the children of Israel, “How long will you neglect to go in to possess the land, which the LORD, the God of your fathers, has given you?
verses.arminianNotes: How long will you neglect to go in? Arminian readers hear a rebuke of spiritual sluggishness, a warning that believers can fail to take hold of what God offers through delay or complacency.
verses.reformedNotes: The land is described as already given by the God of your fathers. Reformed readers see the rebuke as calling the tribes to act on a promise already secured, so their neglect is a failure to receive grace, not a lack of it.

verses.text: Appoint for yourselves three men from each tribe. I will send them, and they shall arise, walk through the land, and describe it according to their inheritance; then they shall come to me.
verses.arminianNotes: Three men from each tribe are to survey the land. Arminian readers note the shared responsibility, with each tribe taking part in the work that prepares for its own inheritance.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see an orderly process under Joshua’s direction, combining human planning with the coming lot. The survey shows that trusting God’s providence does not exclude careful work.

verses.text: They shall divide it into seven portions. Judah shall live in his borders on the south, and the house of Joseph shall live in their borders on the north.
verses.arminianNotes: The land is to be divided into seven portions, with Judah in the south and Joseph in the north already settled. Arminian readers see the remaining tribes being given a fair and defined process for receiving their share.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note how the existing allotments frame the remaining land. God’s distribution unfolds in stages, each building on what he has already given, so the remaining tribes receive land shaped by his earlier provision.

verses.text: You shall survey the land into seven parts, and bring the description here to me; and I will cast lots for you here before the LORD our God.
verses.arminianNotes: Joshua will cast lots before the LORD our God. Arminian readers often frame the lot as God’s chosen way of guiding Israel in that era, an act of trust in which the people accept his decision as fair.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see the lot as an expression of God’s providence, in line with Proverbs 16:33. The phrase before the LORD marks the decision as his, not Joshua’s, so that no tribe could charge favoritism.

verses.text: However, the Levites have no portion among you; for the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance. Gad, Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their inheritance east of the Jordan, which Moses the servant of the LORD gave them.”
verses.arminianNotes: The Levites have no land because the priesthood of the LORD is their inheritance (compare Numbers 18:20). Arminian readers see a reminder that the greatest inheritance is God himself, a truth they apply to every believer’s life.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers note that the Levites’ portion shows that nearness to God surpasses any territory. The eastern tribes are also mentioned, completing the picture of a whole people provided for by God’s word through Moses.

verses.text: The men arose and went. Joshua commanded those who went to survey the land, saying, “Go walk through the land, survey it, and come again to me. I will cast lots for you here before the LORD in Shiloh.”
verses.arminianNotes: The men are told to walk the land and survey it. Arminian readers note that obedience begins with practical steps, walking through the land God has promised and taking its measure.
verses.reformedNotes: Joshua restates that the lots will be cast at Shiloh in the LORD’s presence. Reformed readers see the repetition as stressing that the outcome rests with God, while the survey prepares the ground for his decision.

verses.text: The men went and passed through the land, and surveyed it by cities into seven portions in a book. They came to Joshua to the camp at Shiloh.
verses.arminianNotes: The surveyors write the land by cities into seven portions in a book. Arminian readers note the care taken to give each tribe an accurate and fair description of its possible inheritance.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers observe that the written description becomes the basis for the lot. The orderly record shows that God’s people work with diligence even as they wait on his decision.

verses.text: Joshua cast lots for them in Shiloh before the LORD. There Joshua divided the land to the children of Israel according to their divisions.
verses.arminianNotes: Joshua casts lots and divides the land according to the tribes’ divisions. Arminian readers see the tribes receiving their portions through a process they had all agreed to and helped prepare.
verses.reformedNotes: Reformed readers see God’s hand in the outcome, so that each tribe receives what he appoints. Some also note the later use of the lot in Acts 1:26, while recognizing that Scripture does not present it as a pattern for all decisions.
